dataset.name: Brennan & Hale 2019 Alice in Wonderland EEG
dataset.events_source: GitHub nemarDatasets/nm000180 main and v1.1.3 (SHA-identical events/participants/build_events)
dataset.stimulus: Chapter 1 Alice's Adventures in Wonderland, 12 WAV segments, shared across subjects

rules: Primary scientific cohort is the 27 analyzed=yes subjects with 2129 word events.
Do not expand the headline result to 31 until the 27-subject baseline is reported.
The 4 partial analyzed subjects may appear only in a labeled sensitivity table; they lack segment 12 / sentences 80-84.
The 39 events-available set is a sensitivity set, not the Brennan-analyzed cohort.
The 6 EEG recordings without events cannot be decoded.
Do not mix excluded high_noise/low_comprehension subjects into the primary cohort.

task.name: sentence_retrieval_2to5s
task.metric: retrieval Top-1 and operating_k Top-k against sentence text embeddings
task.forbidden_primary_task: word-level closed-set classification over 601 lowercased types

epoching.reason: median inter-word gap on sub-001 is -0.00185 s; ~1160 overlapping word-duration windows

task.channel_policy: use EEG channels only; drop VEOG and AUD/Aux5
task.preprocess: native-rate FIR 1-40 Hz before epoch and downsample; Autoreject/ICA with real sfreq/highpass
task.label_normalization: join words on space; map SUB (U+001A) and curly apostrophes to ASCII apostrophe
task.encoding_defect: sentence_id 65 word 2 on events.tsv is U+001A + 's' (likely it's); normalize before embedding

sentences.text: thought Alice without pictures or conversation
when suddenly a White Rabbit with pink eyes ran close by
that she ought to have wondered at this
and burning with curiosity she ran across the field after it
First she tried to look down and make out what she was coming to
but to her great disappointment it was empty she did not like to drop the jar
even if I fell off the top of the house Which was very likely TRUE
must be getting somewhere near the center of the earth
still it was good practice to say it over
it ll never do to ask perhaps I shall see it written up somewhere
Down down down There was nothing else to do
I hope they ll remember her saucer of milk at tea time
you see as she could nt answer either question
it did nt much matter which way she put it
and the White Rabbit was still in sight hurrying down
I think I could if I only know how to begin
There seemed to be no use in waiting by the little door
but the wise little Alice was not going to do that in a hurry
and that if you cut your finger very deeply with a knife it usually bleeds
and she had never forgotten that if you drink much from a bottle marked poison
it's almost certain to disagree with you sooner or later

she felt a little nervous about this for it might end you know

but it was too slippery and when she had tired herself out with trying
Soon her eye fell on a little glass box that was lying under the table
to be sure this generally happens when one eats cake

splits.session_note: Each subject has one continuous recording. session_id may be labeled {subject}_run-01 but MUST NOT be used as a cross-session fold.

protocol_A_loso_same_stimulus.name: LOSO-same-stimulus
protocol_A_loso_same_stimulus.what_it_measures: cross-subject generalization to the same Alice chapter-1 stimulus, not zero-shot semantics
protocol_A_loso_same_stimulus.sensitivity_31: optional extra table; partial subjects omit sentences 80 and 84

protocol_B_stimulus_block.name: stimulus-block holdout
protocol_B_stimulus_block.buffer_rule: Drop any train epoch whose [onset - 1.0, offset + 1.0] overlaps a held-out sentence window.
protocol_B_stimulus_block.what_it_measures: generalization to unseen story time / unseen sentences under the same listeners
protocol_B_stimulus_block.partial_subjects: Exclude sub-026/034/035/036 from this protocol because they lack segment 12 test items 80 and 84.

sensitivity_hold_11_12_only.note: thinner test set; not the primary block split

banned: random split of epochs from the same recording into train and test
using word type identity as the primary metric
claiming cross-session results from a single continuous run
training on overlapping 1 s-buffered windows of held-out sentences
